data.title: Earnings Troubles May Signal Larger Issues for Saudi Automotive Services (TADAWUL:4050) Shareholders
data.description:
A lackluster earnings announcement from Saudi Automotive Services Company (TADAWUL:4050) last week didn't sink the stock price. However, we believe that investors should be aware of some underlying factors which may be of concern.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Zooming In On Saudi Automotive Services' Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Saudi Automotive Services has an accrual ratio of -0.18 for the year to September 2026. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of ر.س513m, well over the ر.س34.2m it reported in profit. Saudi Automotive Services shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months. However, that's not all there is to consider. We can see that unusual items have impacted its statutory profit, and therefore the accrual ratio.

Check out our latest analysis for Saudi Automotive Services

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

While the accrual ratio might bode well, we also note that Saudi Automotive Services' profit was boosted by unusual items worth ر.س117m in the last twelve months. While it's always nice to have higher profit, a large contribution from unusual items sometimes dampens our enthusiasm. We ran the numbers on most publicly listed companies worldwide, and it's very common for unusual items to be once-off in nature. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. We can see that Saudi Automotive Services' positive unusual items were quite significant relative to its profit in the year to September 2026. As a result, we can surmise that the unusual items are making its statutory profit significantly stronger than it would otherwise be.

Our Take On Saudi Automotive Services' Profit Performance

Saudi Automotive Services' profits got a boost from unusual items, which indicates they might not be sustained and yet its accrual ratio still indicated solid cash conversion, which is promising. Based on these factors, it's hard to tell if Saudi Automotive Services' profits are a reasonable reflection of its underlying profitability. With this in mind, we wouldn't consider investing in a stock unless we had a thorough understanding of the risks. Every company has risks, and we've spotted 3 warning signs for Saudi Automotive Services (of which 1 is a bit unpleasant!) you should know about.

  • The agreement underscores the scale of GE Aerospace’s installed base and service pipeline, reinforcing how large multiyear engine contracts can shape workload, capital needs, and long-term aftermarket revenue visibility.

General Electric Investment Narrative Recap

To own General Electric, you need to be comfortable with a concentrated aviation story built on a large installed base and long service contracts, while accepting exposure to airframe partners and heavy R&D. The near term swing factor remains execution in commercial engines and services, particularly how efficiently GE converts its reported US$52.6b of revenue into cash while managing supply chain constraints.

The biggest current operational risk is still tied to Boeing production issues, as highlighted by Zdend, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, who flags GE’s dependence on new aircraft deliveries for its future installed base. Recent headlines around building demolition and site clean up look immaterial to that cash and delivery equation.

The most relevant recent item for potential catalysts is the Industrial Select Sector SPDR ETF lifting its GE exposure to 6.38% of assets. That change does not alter the underlying business. However, it reinforces how central GE Aerospace has become within the US industrial complex at a time when earnings are forecast to grow 10.21% a year and the P/E of 36.8x reflects a high level of execution success already in the price.

This heightened ETF presence could increase trading attention around key operational milestones, especially any updates on R&D spend for next generation engines that Zdend views as a major future cash demand. It also sharpens the focus on whether management can keep earnings quality high while carrying a significant debt load and funding large development programs without eroding that aerospace centric thesis.

Zdend sets a US$307.00 fair value for General Electric as the result of GE Aerospace’s concentrated aviation focus, its large commercial engine and services backlog, and the long-duration, contract-based cash flows generated by its aftermarket model and perceived pricing power.

Does adidas Look Pricey on Earnings?

The P/E ratio suits adidas because earnings remain the core way investors judge how well the brand converts sales into profit. At a current P/E of 18.4x, the stock trades at a premium to the Luxury industry average of about 14.8x and above a peer group level near 13.1x. That means every €1 of adidas earnings is priced more expensively than the typical competitor in its sector.

data.title: Here's Why KEI Industries (NSE:KEI) Has Caught The Eye Of Investors
data.description:
It's common for many investors, especially those who are inexperienced, to buy shares in companies with a good story even if these companies are loss-making. But as Peter Lynch said in One Up On Wall Street, 'Long shots almost never pay off.' While a well funded company may sustain losses for years, it will need to generate a profit eventually, or else investors will move on and the company will wither away.

Despite being in the age of tech-stock blue-sky investing, many investors still adopt a more traditional strategy; buying shares in profitable companies like KEI Industries (NSE:KEI). While this doesn't necessarily speak to whether it's undervalued, the profitability of the business is enough to warrant some appreciation - especially if its growing.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

How Fast Is KEI Industries Growing?

The market is a voting machine in the short term, but a weighing machine in the long term, so you'd expect share price to follow earnings per share (EPS) outcomes eventually. Therefore, there are plenty of investors who like to buy shares in companies that are growing EPS. Impressively, KEI Industries has grown EPS by 24% per year, compound, in the last three years. If the company can sustain that sort of growth, we'd expect shareholders to come away satisfied.

It's often helpful to take a look at earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) margins, as well as revenue growth, to get another take on the quality of the company's growth. KEI Industries maintained stable EBIT margins over the last year, all while growing revenue 25% to ₹134b. That's a real positive.

You can take a look at the company's revenue and earnings growth trend, in the chart below. Click on the chart to see the exact numbers.

See our latest analysis for KEI Industries

In investing, as in life, the future matters more than the past. So why not check out this free interactive visualization of KEI Industries' forecast profits?

Are KEI Industries Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?

It's a necessity that company leaders act in the best interest of shareholders and so insider investment always comes as a reassurance to the market. Shareholders will be pleased by the fact that insiders own KEI Industries shares worth a considerable sum. Notably, they have an enviable stake in the company, worth ₹61b. Coming in at 17% of the business, that holding gives insiders a lot of influence, and plenty of reason to generate value for shareholders. Very encouraging.

Does KEI Industries Deserve A Spot On Your Watchlist?

For growth investors, KEI Industries' raw rate of earnings growth is a beacon in the night. This EPS growth rate is something the company should be proud of, and so it's no surprise that insiders are holding on to a considerable chunk of shares. Fast growth and confident insiders should be enough to warrant further research, so it would seem that it's a good stock to follow. We don't want to rain on the parade too much, but we did also find 1 warning sign for KEI Industries that you need to be mindful of.

There's always the possibility of doing well buying stocks that are not growing earnings and do not have insiders buying shares. But for those who consider these important metrics, we encourage you to check out companies that do have those features.
